MUQATIL:30:54-57/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:54-57/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:54-57/r3.claim: On Resurrection Day criminals swear they stayed in their graves only an hour; this mirrors their worldly denial of resurrection.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r5.claim: The criminals are polytheists who swear they remained only an hour in worldly life and in their graves.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r6.claim: Their claim reflects how they had been diverted in worldly life from belief in resurrection.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#3/r1.claim: When they rise from their graves, the guilty swear they stayed no more than an hour.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#3/r2.claim: They are deceived now just as they lied in worldly life; afaka can also mean divert from truth and good, and a maʾfūka land is deprived of rain.

TAB-FULL:v18p527/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p527/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p527/r1.claim: When the Hour comes, disbelieving criminals swear they stayed in their graves less than an hour, as they had lied knowingly in worldly life.

TAB-FULL:v18p527/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p527/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p527/r2.claim: Qatada says they lied in worldly life and were turned away from truth toward falsehood.

ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r1.claim: The Hour means the time when Resurrection occurs; criminals swear they remained in their graves only an hour, lying without proof.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p278/r6.claim: The verse does not deny punishment in the grave; the Prophet authentically sought refuge from it and instructed others to do so.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NAHHAS:v3p278/r7.claim: He reports that when Umm Ḥabība asked God to preserve her husband, father, and brother, the Prophet said lifespans and provisions are fixed and advised her to seek refuge from Hell or grave punishment.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p278/r8.claim: One view says the dead mean the quiet interval before resurrection and call it an hour because they did little; another says worldly life seems like an hour because it passes, despite their claiming knowledge of the unseen.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p278/r9.claim: Ka-dhālika kānū yuʾfakūn means they used to lie in worldly life; the Qur’an rejects the claim that people cannot lie at the resurrection by describing them swearing falsely there.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r1.claim: The criminals who swear they tarried only an hour are unbelievers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r2.claim: They describe worldly time as only an hour, minimizing it after seeing the Hereafter.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r3.claim: Alternatively, they mean their time in graves between death and resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r4.claim: Kazālika means thus or in this way.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r5.claim: Yūfakūn means they lied in worldly life.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r6.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p323/r6.claim: Alternatively, they were turned from belief in resurrection in worldly life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes say criminals swear at the Resurrection that they stayed in their graves for only an hour.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r2.claim: Qatada instead says they will claim to have lived in the world for only an hour; the author rejects this because the next verse supports the grave interpretation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes كذلك as comparing their present oath to their earlier false speech, since they swore without reliable knowledge.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says their claim of only an hour was false just as they had lied in worldly life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r5.claim: Muqatil says they denied resurrection in worldly life and now lie that they spent only an hour in their graves.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba says they lie now as before and explains أفك as being turned away from truth and goodness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r7.claim: Muqatil and others explain that seeing the afterlife made them regard their stay in the world or graves as very short.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r8.claim: The author says they deliberately swear an unexcused, plain lie so believers can recognize their falsehood and infer that their former idolatry and unbelief were lies too.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84#2/r9.claim: The passive يؤفكون indicates that God turns them from truth in their oath just as they were turned away from faith in worldly life, affirming divine decree; an active form would have expressed their own lying.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:54-58/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:54-58/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:54-58/r2.claim: At resurrection the disbelievers swear they remained in their graves less than an hour, continuing their worldly habit of lying.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r1.claim: At resurrection, polytheists swear they stayed in the world less than an hour because worldly life seems brief beside the Hereafter.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r2.claim: They say they remained in their graves for less than an hour.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p278/r3.claim: They were turned away from truth in life; their false claim, like their denial of resurrection, is exposed by God’s decree.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r6.claim: The criminals swear stubbornly and without knowledge that they stayed under the earth less than an hour, continuing their worldly habit of false reasoning; yufakun means turned from truth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r7.claim: Some say they mean their worldly life seemed brief after they saw the afterlife; Ibn Atiyya rejects this because the verse says they were habitually turned away from truth.

TABRISI:30:51-55/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:51-55/r9.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:30:51-55/r9.claim: The criminals swear at resurrection that they remained in their graves for only an hour; this interpretation is attributed to al-Kalbi and Muqatil.

TABRISI:30:55/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:55/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:55/r1.claim: The criminals may mean they spent only an hour in worldly life because they regard its duration as insignificant, or only an hour after the punishment of the grave ceased; al-Jubbāʾī and Matta hold the latter.

TABRISI:30:55/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:55/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:55/r2.claim: To explain false oaths despite certain knowledge in the afterlife, Abu Ali and Abu Hashim say they swear according to their conjecture, since they did not know how long they remained in the graves.

TABRISI:30:55/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:55/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن الإخشيد
TABRISI:30:55/r3.claim: Another answer is that their oaths could occur before their minds were fully developed.

TABRISI:30:55/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:55/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:55/r4.claim: The author rejects using this verse to deny punishment in the grave, since they may mean that only an hour passed after God’s punishment there.

TABRISI:30:55/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:55/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:55/r5.claim: Yuʾfakūn can mean that they lied in worldly life or that ignorance turned them away from truth in both abodes.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r1.claim: In the Quran, الساعة means the moment when Resurrection occurs; it is indefinite because no one knows which hour it will be.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r2.claim: The criminals are polytheists who swear they remained in their graves less than an hour.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r3.claim: أفك means a person was turned away from truth, so their claim is a lie as their worldly claims were.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that God exposes them before believers on Judgment Day by making them swear to something whose falsity is evident, confirming their worldly lies.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r1.claim: The criminals who swear are the polytheists.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r10.claim: The Quran also says that they will swear to God as they swear to people and falsely think they have something to stand on.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r11.claim: Another passage depicts their claim that they were not polytheists and exposes their lie.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r2.claim: The claim that they remained only an hour does not disprove punishment in the grave, which is established by authentic Prophetic reports and the Prophet's instruction to seek refuge from it.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r3.claim: He reports that the Prophet heard Umm Ḥabība ask for blessing in her husband, father, and brother, then directed her to seek refuge from Hellfire and grave punishment; Qurtubi says the reports are well-known in Muslim, Bukhari, and others.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r4.claim: One interpretation says there must be an interval of stillness before Resurrection, so they describe their stay then as only an hour.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r5.claim: Alternatively, they mean worldly life, which seems brief because it has vanished; this resembles the description in al-Nāziʿāt.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r6.claim: They swear about the unseen without knowing; kādhālika kānū yuʾfakūn says they used to lie in worldly life, and afaka means to turn someone away from truth and good.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r7.claim: The word maʾfūka can describe land deprived of rain.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r8.speaker: جماعة من أهل النظر
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r8.claim: Some rationalists claim lying cannot occur on Resurrection Day; Qurtubi rejects this because the Quran says they are diverted from truth and depicts them swearing falsely then.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:55/r9.claim: Their false oath on that day repeats their habitual turning away from truth in worldly life.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r1.claim: The Hour is named because it comes at the world's final hour or arrives suddenly and became its established name.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r2.claim: The criminals may mean their time in the world, in graves, or between worldly destruction and resurrection; a report gives forty from the end of the world to resurrection, with its unit unspecified.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:55-56/r3.claim: They say not even an hour because the stay seems brief beside their punishment or because they forgot it; in life they were diverted from truthful accounting.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r1.claim: The Hour is so named because it occurs in the final hour of worldly time, or because it arrives suddenly like an appointed hour.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r2.claim: The oath's answer is “they remained no more than an hour”; there is no pause after “the guilty swear.” They may mean the grave or worldly life, minimized from fear, forgetfulness, or lying.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#4/r3.claim: Their worldly habit of turning from truth to falsehood included denying any life beyond this one.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r1.claim: The answer “we have reached Khurāsān” illustrates a reply whose conditional premise is supplied by context; when the fāʾ can simply coordinate, an omitted condition need not be invented.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r2.claim: “You do not know” may mean they neglected seeking and following truth, or that they did not know or recognize resurrection and thus ask for respite in Hell.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p402/r3.claim: “On that day” refers to the day when the unbelievers swear and the people of knowledge answer them.

SAMIN-DURR:30:55/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:55/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:30:55/r1.claim: ما لبثوا answers يقسم by sense; direct quotation would say ما لبثنا. كذلك means they were deluded in the same way.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328/r1.claim: Disbelievers display ignorance in both lives: they worship idols here and later swear they stayed only an hour, hoping to escape the proof against them.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r7.claim: The Hour recreates in less than a blink what unfolded gradually over thousands of years; it is called the Hour because it is easy for God.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r8.claim: Criminals will swear that they remained in the world and barzakh only a brief hour, speaking from ignorance and their habit of being diverted from truth into doubt and falsehood.

DURR-FULL:v6p502/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p502/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p502/r1.claim: Criminals call worldly life less than an hour because it seems short when they see the afterlife; Qatada says they were accustomed to lying in this life.

BURSEVI:v7p43/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p43/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p43/r1.claim: The Hour is named because it occurs in the final hour of worldly time, or because it arrives suddenly; the name became proper through frequent use.

BURSEVI:v7p43/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p43/r2.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v7p43/r2.claim: The criminals swear that they remained in their graves for only one hour, a tiny span of time, through forgetfulness, lying, or guesswork.

BURSEVI:v7p43/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p43/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p43/r3.claim: Although some take their brief stay to mean worldly life, the author prefers the grave, since the statement is tied to Resurrection Day and their worldly stay was not so short.

BURSEVI:v7p43/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p43/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p43/r4.claim: Their claim is like their worldly denial of resurrection and oath that God would not raise the dead; they are diverted from truth into falsehood and lie in both lives.

BURSEVI:v7p43/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p43/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p43/r5.claim: Truth casts faith and sincerity, while falsehood casts disbelief and hypocrisy; these roots yield truthful testimony from believers and further lies from unbelievers at resurrection.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the claim occurs when punishment is interrupted and they lie to minimize their stay, or forget it in terror; they may compare with coming punishment.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.claim: They may call life an hour because they gained nothing: much without benefit is little, while little with benefit is much, expressing regret for wasted life.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.claim: The passage uses complete paronomasia between Resurrection and an hour of time; inflection and the article do not spoil it because the first became a proper name.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ḥajar proposes a second Quranic pun treating the second ‘eyes’ as insight; al-Ālūsī rejects it as metaphor and irregular plural of baṣīrah.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.claim: The clause describes persistent denial or their astonishing delusion about life’s length now that it was an hour, to spur them from worldly attachment; God, Satan, or desire may be the agent, but their choices remain responsible, and one view says unbelievers can lie after death.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r1.claim: Al-sāʿah means Resurrection, named as the final worldly hour or because it arrives suddenly; ‘rising’ means its existence or creatures standing in it.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say criminals swear they stayed only an hour in graves after death; al-Ālūsī prefers this because the stay continues until Resurrection.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r3.claim: Qatāda instead says they mean they spent no more than an hour in worldly life.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p59/r4.claim: Another view concerns the interval before resurrection. Abū Hurayra’s report says it is forty but omits the unit; al-Ālūsī says only God knows and rejects claimed consensus for forty years.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p60/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p60/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p60/r1.claim: Some use this verse to deny punishment in the grave, but al-Ālūsī says that inference is unsound.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r5.claim: This fourth resumption returns to signs in creation to establish God's power and make resurrection intelligible, paralleling 30:48; the following reference to the Hour confirms the link.

TABATABAI:30:54-56/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r4.claim: The criminals' short estimate of their stay follows their lifelong distortion of truth: they misread the interval between death and resurrection as only an hour of worldly time.

TABATABAI:30:54-56/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r5.claim: They judge the resurrection by the world's order because they are absorbed in earthly life and know little beyond it; thus the truth appears false to them, with no excuse.

TABATABAI:30:54-56/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r6.claim: 'They were turned away' means they persistently turn from truth to falsehood, treating clear proofs as fables when called to the truth.

ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n49/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n49/r1.claim: Asad inserts the implied death and resurrection to connect this passage with the preceding context and verses 11-16 and 27.

ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n50/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n50/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n50/r1.claim: The Qur'an treats earthly time as relative: life is infinitesimal beside the timeless hereafter, while sinners use its supposed brevity as a self-excuse.

ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n50/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n50/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:55#n50/r2.claim: Yu'fikun literally evokes being turned away from truth; here it describes the sinners' lifelong self-deception.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:55/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:55/r1.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:55/r1.claim: Because verse 55 does not say where they stayed, interpreters suggest the world, graves, or the interval between the world’s end and resurrection.

STUDYQURAN:30:55/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r1.claim: The guilty’s claim that they tarried an hour may mean their experience of the period in the grave before Resurrection.

STUDYQURAN:30:55/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r2.claim: Alternatively, the claim may refer to their earthly lifetime, which seems like an hour or less beside the Hereafter’s eternity.

STUDYQURAN:30:55/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r3.claim: The guilty may make the claim in ignorance or to argue that the evidence against them is insufficient.

STUDYQURAN:30:55/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r4.speaker: Iṣ
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r4.claim: Yuʾfakū literally means “turned away” and connotes a negative turning from truth toward falsehood, such as lying or ugly deeds.

STUDYQURAN:30:55/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r5.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:30:55/r5.claim: Yuʾfakū can also mean “thus were they deluded,” describing their mistaken view of this world’s relation to the Hereafter.

STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.claim: The sūrah closes by recalling that disbelievers’ hearts are sealed and urging steadfastness when facing them.
